newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador takes first step towards convertibility.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador takes first step towards convertibility.

text.p: Ecuador took its first step towards currency Convertibility Tuesday, by announcing new limitations for Central Bank operations in money markets.
The Central Bank issued a statement saying it will cease the injection of short-term liquidity into the money market via sovereign or Central Bank paper.

"Given the national government's decision to enter into a system of Convertibility at a date to be announced by the president, the Central Bank will only inject sucres into the financial system at the same rate as the issuing institution buys dollars," it said.

The Central Bank intervened in the money markets Tuesday after allowing the exchange rate to move to the middle of the currency band Monday. The dollar rose 13 sucres, or 0.48 percent, to close Tuesday at 3,506 sucres.
The Central Bank also abandoned its role of allocating funds to banks, leading to a seven percentage point rise in the overnight rate to 35 percent.
"This is a first step towards Convertibility," economist Fidel Jarmillo, head of the private consultancy Multiplica, told reuters.
"It means we can settle into the new system the government wants and put pressure on the market to get rid of the dollars they bought in the past week."

Local and international financial markets are eagerly awaiting the announcement, scheduled for December 1, of a major package of economic measures from the government of the country's populist new President Abdala Bucaram.
The central plank of policy is to be Convertibility, along the lines of the system in place in Argentina since 1991 that pegs the Argentine peso at par to the dollar.
While many local economists are keen on accompanying talk of fiscal discipline, they express doubts about the technical ability of Bucaram's government to apply such policies.
"There is a dichotomy between the program on paper, which is consistent and professional, and the actors who would apply it who lack credibility," said Jaramillo.
